rfi.title: How music became a 'balm' for New York in the aftermath of 9/11
rfi.description: The 9/11 attacks changed not only New York's skyline but the music Americans used to make sense of tragedy. From Bruce Springsteen's songs of collective grief to Jay-Z's defiance and the Beastie Boys' love letter to their city, musicians responded in very different ways – helping to shape how the attacks are remembered 25 years later.

rfi.title: As catches dwindle, Congo River fishermen turn to plastic waste
rfi.description: On the Congo River, plastic is becoming the catch of the day. Some fishermen around Kinshasa, capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo, can now make more money pulling plastic from the water than catching fish, as declining catches and growing waste pollution threaten an artisanal way of life.

rfi.title: From townships to TikTok, South Africa's amapiano gets the world dancing
rfi.description: Amapiano dancers across South Africa are helping a sound born in the country's black townships reach audiences far beyond its borders – one viral challenge at a time. Short routines filmed in homes, schools and public spaces are spreading across social media, giving musicians another way to promote a genre that's now a global hit.

rfi.title: Before its peak, El Nino brings failed crops and empty fishing nets
rfi.description: El Nino is already disrupting livelihoods and weather patterns around the world as one of the strongest events in decades continues to intensify. With its peak still months away, scientists warn the powerful Pacific climate phenomenon will bring more drought and flooding into 2027, while human-caused global warming is making some of its effects more severe.

rfi.title: How 100 days of record ocean heat is reshaping life in and around the seas
rfi.description: Global oceans have endured 100 consecutive days of record average heat, as human-driven climate change pushes temperatures higher and puts growing pressure on marine life. Scientists say prolonged warming is disrupting fisheries, damaging coral reefs, raising sea levels and threatening economies that depend on healthy seas.

zeit.description: Die Basketballerinnen aus den USA haben sich ihren 12. Mal Weltmeistertitel gesichert. Im Finale gegen Frankreich holte das Team seinen anfänglichen Rückstand auf.

zeit.title: Unfall in Schwaben: Frontalkollision auf Bundesstraße - zwei Schwerverletzte
Wahlen in Niedersachsen: Landeschef Schledde: «AfD seit heute Kommunalpartei»
Grüne und CDU in Stichwahl: SPD verliert Göttinger Rathaus
Ex-Torwart von Hannover 96: Pokalheld Sievers verpasst Stichwahl um Bürgermeisteramt
Kommunalwahl: Amtsinhaber in Braunschweig muss in die Stichwahl
Kommunalwahl in Niedersachsen: Niedersachsen hat gewählt - Hochrechnung sieht CDU vorn
American Football: St. Brown mit Touchdown bei Lions-Sieg in NFL
»Tatort: König in Gelb«: Der Mann ist definitiv ein Mann
zeit.description: Mit einem neuen »Tatort« aus Hannover endet die Sommerpause. Schwierige Ermittlungssituation: Ist der Täter möglicherweise dement?

zeit.title: Kommunalwahl in Niedersachsen: Erste Hochrechnung sieht CDU bei Kommunalwahl in Niedersachsen vorn
zeit.description: In Niedersachsen hat die CDU sich bei der Kommunalwahl verschlechtert, bleibt aber weiterhin stärkste Kraft. Nur die AfD und die Linke können ihre Ergebnisse verbessern.

zeit.title: Parlamentswahl in Schweden: Regierungsblock und Opposition laut Hochrechnung beinahe gleichauf
zeit.description: Die Sozialdemokraten sind bei der Parlamentswahl in Schweden ersten Zahlen zufolge stärkste Kraft. Der rechte und der linke Block kommen auf fast gleich viele Sitze.

zeit.title: Angriffe auf die Ukraine: Ukraine meldet russische Angriffe auf Bahnnetz
zeit.description: Die Ukraine wirft Russland systematische Angriffe auf ihr Bahnnetz vor. Ein Angriff nahe der Grenze zu Polen könnte laut der Bahn einem Diplomatenzug gegolten haben.

zeit.title: David Sedaris: »Mein Vater war ein Arschloch, aber eine großartige Figur«
zeit.description: Der Schriftsteller David Sedaris interessiert sich für jeden Menschen, dem er begegnet, und verschont keinen in seinen Büchern. Sein Trick: stets unberechenbar bleiben.

zeit.title: Unterstützung für Kanzler Merz: Söder und Kretschmer warnen vor Scheitern der Bundesregierung
zeit.description: CSU-Chef Markus Söder und CDU-Vize Michael Kretschmer mahnen nach der Wahl in Sachsen-Anhalt zu Eile bei den Reformen. Jetzt sei nicht die Zeit für Personaldebatten.

france24fr.title: Santé mentale en Afrique : comment briser le tabou du suicide ?
france24fr.description: Près de 150 millions de personnes vivent avec des troubles de santé mentale en Afrique. Pourtant, l’accès aux soins reste très insuffisant et le suicide demeure entouré de tabous. Pourquoi le continent est-il particulièrement vulnérable ? Comment mieux prévenir, libérer la parole et rapprocher les soins des populations ? Entretien avec le Dr Adelard Kakunze, responsable technique des maladies non transmissibles, traumatismes et santé mentale à Africa CDC

france24fr.title: Au Yémen, les Houthis font état d'une cinquantaine de frappes saoudiennes
france24fr.description: Les Houthis ont rapporté dimanche d'une cinquantaine de frappes saoudiennes au Yémen, notamment sur leur fief dans le nord du pays, quelques heures après avoir revendiqué une attaque contre une base militaire en Arabie saoudite. Ryad n'a pas confirmé les frappes au Yémen et communique par ailleurs peu sur celles menées par les Houthis contre le royaume.

france24fr.title: Mondial de basket : les Bleues s'inclinent en finale face aux invincibles Américaines
france24fr.description: Les basketteuses françaises se sont lourdement inclinées 97 à 79 dimanche soir en finale de la Coupe du monde à Berlin contre les États-Unis, invaincues depuis 20 ans en compétition majeure (Jeux olympiques et Mondial) et désormais quintuples championnes du monde en titre.

france24fr.title: Lukas Aubin : " le virilisme d'Etat de Poutine s'est transformé en instrument géopolitique"
france24fr.description: Vladimir Poutine tente de contrôler l'intime, la sexualité et les mœurs, pour contrôler la société et servir son pouvoir: c'est la thèse développée dans un livre qui vient de paraître : "Le sexe de poutine: genre, pouvoir et contre culture en Russie" (éditions Textuel). Son auteur, Lukas Aubin, directeur de recherche à l'IRIS et spécialiste de la Russie, était l'Invité d'Au Cœur de l'Info.

france24fr.title: Législatives en Suède : la gauche et l'extrême droite au coude-à-coude, le dépouillement en cours
france24fr.description: Alors que le dépouillement se poursuit dimanche soir après les législatives en Suède, la coalition de droite du Premier ministre Ulf Kristersson, soutenue par l'extrême droite, reste au coude-à-coude avec l'opposition de centre-gauche. Près de huit millions d’électeurs étaient appelés aux urnes.

france24fr.title: La gauche ou des ministres d'extrême droite? La Suède à l'heure du choix
france24fr.description: Le retour de la gauche au pouvoir? Ou l'entrée fracassante de l'extrême droite au gouvernement ? Des millions de Suédois votent dimanche pour des élections législatives cruciales, à l'issue très incertaine.

france24fr.title: L'Intelligence artificielle, réelle menace existentielle pour l'humanité ?
france24fr.description: Raphaël Millière, Maître de conférences à l'université d'Oxford au Royaume-Uni, est notre invité.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : des frappes russes près de la frontière polonaise, Varsovie dénonce une "escalade"
france24fr.description: La compagnie ukrainienne de chemins de fer a averti dimanche qu'une "attaque systémique" était "en cours" contre le rail à travers l'Ukraine, signalant une frappe de drone russe à proximité de la frontière polonaise sur un train de voyageurs. Donald Tusk a mis en garde contre une intensification des attaques russes en Ukraine dans les prochaines semaines.

france24fr.title: Naufrage d'un ferry en Indonésie : au moins 6 morts et 130 disparus
france24fr.description: Six personnes sont mortes, 130 sont toujours portées disparues dimanche et 107 ont pu être secourues après qu'un ferry reliant les îles indonésiennes de Java et de Bornéo a chaviré en raison de mauvaises conditions météo, ont indiqué les services de secours et des responsables des transports.

france24fr.title: Paris : le Village international de la gastronomie fête ses 10 ans
france24fr.description: Anne-Laure Descombin, présidente-fondatrice du Village international de la gastronomie à Paris, est notre invitée.

france24fr.title: Céline Dion émue, son public enchanté : 2h de show incroyable
france24fr.description: "On ne change pas", "All by Myself", "Pour que tu m'aimes encore"... Bouleversée par son retour sur scène après six ans d'absence, Céline Dion a enchaîné les tubes samedi soir pour le coup d'envoi de sa série de concerts près de Paris, une renaissance après des années marquées par la maladie.

france24fr.title: La Mostra de Venise récompense "Woman Unknown" et le documentaire "Naza"
france24fr.description: Le faible nombre de réalisatrices en compétition à la Mostra de Venise avait provoqué un tollé: le jury présidé par Maggie Gyllenhaal a décidé samedi de récompenser l'une d'entre elles, May el-Toukhy, pour "Woman Unknown" sur le destin d'une femme au Danemark dans l'immédiat après-guerre. Un documentaire choc israélien sur Gaza réalisé par les journalistes  d'investigation Yuval Abraham et Rachel Szor, déjà coauteurs du film oscarisé "No Other Land" (2024), a remporté samedi le prix spécial du j

france24fr.title: Guerre au Moyen-Orient : "le prix du baril sera l'arbitre de cette guerre"
france24fr.description: Thierry Bros, professeur à SciencesPo et expert energies, est notre invité.

france24fr.title: Yémen : au moins 76 000 personnes ont fui les combats depuis juillet
france24fr.description: Plus de 2 000 personnes ont fui par bateau depuis jeudi soir le Yémen, en proie à des combats entre forces gouvernementales et les Houthis, vers Djibouti, a affirmé dimanche l'Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIM). Les Houthis, qui contrôlaient jusque-là une grande partie du nord du pays, dont la capitale Sanaa, et Hodeida (ouest), ont progressé sur la côte en quelques jours, s'emparant jeudi de la ville portuaire de Mokha.

france24fr.title: Pendaisons, vengeance et spoliations : trois livres pour raconter les cicatrices de la guerre
france24fr.description: Cette année, la rentrée littéraire fait une place notable aux romans et récits inspirés ou ancrés dans la Seconde Guerre mondiale. France 24 a sélectionné trois ouvrages qui explorent des aspects méconnus de cette période sombre de notre histoire.

france24fr.title: 25 ans du 11-Septembre, victoire de l'AfD en Allemagne, avancée des Houthis : la semaine en images
france24fr.description: Retour sur les temps forts de l'actualité de la semaine écoulée et ses images les plus marquantes : une installation artistique pour les commémorations du 25e anniversaire des attentats du 11-Septembre, les célébrations et contestations après la victoire de l'AfD dans le Land de Saxe-Anhalt en Allemagne, ou encore l'offensive au Yémen des Houthis pro-iraniens, qui se sont emparés d'un point de passage stratégique entre la mer Rouge et le golfe d'Aden.

france24fr.title: Trump fustige les "forces négatives" qui veulent freiner le développement de l'IA
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a dénoncé dimanche les "forces négatives" qui veulent ralentir le développement de l'intelligence artificielle. Cette déclaration intervient alors que les appels à davantage de prudence et de régulation se multiplient, y compris de la part de figures du secteur comme le patron d'Anthropic, Dario Amodei.

france24fr.title: Mondial de basket : les Françaises veulent détrôner la Team USA en finale
france24fr.description: Après leur victoire samedi face à l'Allemagne, hôte du tournoi, les Bleues doivent disputer dimanche soir la finale de la Coupe du monde, une première dans l'histoire du basket français. Face à la Team USA, quadruple tenante du titre, invaincue en tournoi international depuis 20 ans, et octuple médaillée d'or olympique, les Bleues s'attaquent une fois de plus à un monument.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Handelsstreit: Trump hebt Zoll für irischen Whisky auf
nzz.description: Diesen Februar hat der Supreme Court Trumps Zölle für unrechtmässig erklärt. Doch der amerikanische Präsident verursacht mit seinen umstrittenen Zöllen weiter weltweit Turbulenzen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen.

nzz.title: Xherdan Shaqiri wirkt nach dem Trainerwechsel wie verwandelt – er führt den FC Basel in Luzern zum 4:2
nzz.description: Der FCB überzeugt im ersten Spiel nach der Entlassung des Trainers Stephan Lichtsteiner. Die Basler bezwingen den FC Luzern nach frühem Rückstand – Shaqiri trifft doppelt und steuert einen Assist bei.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Aufrufe zur Verlangsamung reichen nicht: KI-Firmen müssen endlich mehr in die Sicherheitsforschung investieren
nzz.description: Plötzlich treten die wichtigsten KI-Unternehmen der Welt auf die Bremse. Dabei haben sie jahrelang auf Leistung gesetzt und die Risiken zu wenig beachtet.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Polen alarmiert nach Angriff auf Zug im ukrainisch-polnischen Grenzgebiet +++ Entwarnung in Litauen: Vermeintliche Drohnensichtung entpuppt sich als Vogelschwarm
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Die Siegesserie ist perfekt: Die 800-Meter-Läuferin Audrey Werro krönt ihr Traumjahr an der Ultimate Championship
nzz.description: Die 22-jährige Schweizerin gewinnt auch ihr letztes Rennen der Saison. Werro überstrahlt damit eine Schweizer Leichtathletik, die so konstant war wie selten.

nzz.title: Trumps «Vizekönig» stösst in Südamerika an seine Grenzen
nzz.description: Marco Rubio besucht erstmals die neuen Verbündeten der USA in Südamerika. Doch Kolumbien, Ecuador und Peru folgen Washington nicht auf ganzer Linie.

nzz.title: Angriff auf die Lebensader: Nach einer Drohnenattacke ist Saudiarabiens wichtigste Pipeline ausser Betrieb
nzz.description: In der Nacht auf Samstag haben mehrere aus dem Irak kommende Drohnen die saudische Ost-West-Pipeline angegriffen. Es ist eine weitere Eskalation im Wirtschaftskrieg am Golf.

nzz.title: Der Brics-Gipfel in Delhi kritisiert die westliche Weltordnung, will aber nicht gegen den Westen sein
nzz.description: Die auf elf Mitglieder angewachsene Staatengruppe versucht die Zusammenarbeit zu stärken. Für eine Abkehr vom Dollar und andere weitreichende Schritte gibt es aber keine Einigkeit. Ihre Grösse ist auch ihr Nachteil.

nzz.title: Jelena Rybakina triumphiert in New York – die Eiskönigin ist im Tennis-Olymp angekommen
nzz.description: Die Kasachin bezwingt ihre Rivalin Aryna Sabalenka im US-Open-Final. In ihrer Heimat verschmäht und begleitet von schweren Vorwürfen gegen ihren Coach, ist sie am Montag die neue Nummer eins.

nzz.title: Die Schweizerinnen sind die Besten des Rests: Julie Derron und Alanis Siffert gewinnen an der Ironman-70.3-Weltmeisterschaft Silber und Bronze
nzz.description: Die Amerikanerin Taylor Knibb gewinnt die 1,9 km Schwimmen, 90 km Radfahren und 21,1 km Laufen in Nizza mit über 4 Minuten Vorsprung.

nzz.title: Indonesische Fähre in Seenot – fast 130 Personen vermisst
nzz.description: Fähren sind im Inselstaat Indonesien ein wichtiges Transportmittel. Zwischen Java und Borneo ist eine von ihnen in Seenot geraten. Dutzende Passagiere konnten durch andere Schiffe gerettet werden.

nzz.title: Fährbrand auf den Philippinen: Zahl der Todesopfer steigt auf 76 – Identifizierung könnte Monate dauern
nzz.description: Bei einem Brand auf einer Fähre vor den Philippinen sind mindestens 76 Menschen ums Leben gekommen, 13 weitere gelten als vermisst. Die Ursache des Feuers ist weiterhin unklar.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Toter nach Angriff auf iranisches Containerschiff
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Nach Alleingängen der KI: Open AI und Anthropic einigen sich auf freiwillige Verlangsamung der KI-Entwicklung
nzz.description: Die Meldungen zu übermächtiger künstlicher Intelligenz überschlagen sich. Nun treten die beiden führenden KI-Labs auf die Bremse. Auch Elon Musks Grok stimmt einer freiwilligen Pause zu. Open AI verzögert zudem seinen Börsengang.

nzz.title: Die Huthi erobern die Meerenge Bab al-Mandab nicht nur zur Schützenhilfe Irans. Sie wollen ihre eigene Kasse mit Milliarden füllen
nzz.description: Jahrelang bauten die Huthi eine Schatten- und Schmuggelwirtschaft auf. Durch ihren jüngsten Feldzug könnten sie nun noch mehr kassieren. Das Problem für Teheran: Je mehr Geld die Huthi haben, desto weniger abhängig sind sie – und desto weniger kontrollierbar.

nzz.title: Die USA suchten ihn, Maduro liess ihn verhaften, doch dann verschwand er:  Die Jagd nach dem «Bolichico» führt in die Schweiz
nzz.description: Die Trump-Regierung hat kürzlich bei den Zürcher Staatsanwälten interveniert, weil sie gegen Alejandro Betancourt ermitteln, der in Venezuela zum wichtigsten Dealmaker geworden ist. Doch im Visier haben die Strafverfolger vor allem auch seinen Cousin.

observador.title: Escócia, Gales e Irlanda do Norte unem-se pela independência
observador.description: Os três primeiros-ministros pró-independência encontram-se esta segunda-feira em Cardiff. Burnham tenta travar a maré, mas Trump e o SNP aumentam a pressão sobre Londres.

observador.title: Morreu o editor belga de BD Yves Schlirf
observador.description: Yves Schlirf, figura chave na explosão da manga japonesa nos países francófonos com best-sellers como "Naruto", morreu este sábado.

observador.title: EUA campeões mundiais femininos de basquetebol pela 5.ª vez
observador.description: Equipa feminina de basquetebol norte-americana sagrou-se pela quinta vez consecutiva campeã mundial, após derrotar a França por 97-79.

observador.title: Marco Silva "passou a ansiedade" à equipa
observador.description: Uma vitória "suadinha" do Benfica, num jogo em que Marco Silva passou "ansiedade" à equipa. Gabriel Alves destaca a reação encarnada e antevê um clássico de força contra técnica" no estádio do Dragão.

observador.title: "Há pessoas que chegam ao aeroporto e vêm para o hospital"
observador.description: A responsável de um dos hospitais mais pressionados explica que 40% dos utentes são estrangeiros e admite que o turismo de saúde "é um problema". Sandra Cavaca tem um plano para atacar o inverno.

observador.title: 21h. Bugalho espera desculpas do PS ao ministro da Educação
observador.description: Brilhante Dias chamou a Fernando Alexandre o “pior ministro da Educação desde o 25 de Abril”. Bugalho espera pedido de desculpas quando todos os alunos tiverem vaga. Ainda, Benfica vence Gil Vicente.

observador.title: "Não vai ser sempre sem sofrer, sempre a marcar cedo..."
observador.description: Treinador do Benfica diz que não foi surpreendido pelo esquema do Gil Vicente mas que nem tudo correu conforme pretendido. No entanto, entre elogios a Echeverri, destacou o "acreditar até ao fim".

observador.title: Adolescente morre no rio Douro em Vila Nova de Gaia
observador.description: Adolescente de 12 anos morreu no rio Douro em Avintes, no concelho de Vila Nova de Gaia. No local estiveram 27 operacionais.

observador.title: Santa Clara vence em Arouca por 2-1
observador.description: Santa Clara bateu o Arouca por 2-1 e subiu provisoriamente ao terceiro lugar do campeonato.

observador.title: GNR atropelado por condutor que desrespeitou ordens
observador.description: Um condutor de motociclo desobedeceu a uma ordem de paragem na zona da Costa da Caparica (Almada) e atropelou um militar da GNR, que sofreu ferimentos ligeiros.

observador.title: "Samuel Soares, guarda-redes de equipa grande."
observador.description: Na opinião de João Pinto, os adeptos encarnados levaram a equipa à vitória. "O Gil Vicente" fez um grande jogo na luz, Prestianni e Pavlidis estiveram em grande e Samuel Soares foi salvador.

observador.title: Oliver Solberg vence Rali do Chile
observador.description: Sueco Oliver Solberg venceu o Rali do Chile e aproximou-se da liderança do Mundial. Toyota conquista assim o 10.º título mundial de construtores.

observador.title: Madrid arranca com teste de táxis áutonomos (sob supervisão)
observador.description: Depois de Londres e Munique, os táxis autónomos (sem necessidade de condutor) vão começar a circular em Madrid. As deslocações serão efectuadas através da plataforma da Uber.

observador.title: Liga: preços dos combustíveis a "estrangular" bombeiros
observador.description: Liga dos Bombeiros Portugueses (LBP) diz que aumento dos combustíveis está a ter um "impacto muito negativo" sobre as corporações de bombeiros, que estão a ser "estranguladas".

observador.title: Nunca desistiram dele e ele continua a recusar desistir
observador.description: No jogo mais complicado da época na Luz frente a um Gil Vicente bem montado e capaz de anular pontos fortes do Benfica, voltou a ser a magia individual de Prestianni a construir a reviravolta (3-1).

observador.title: PIlotos da EasyJet França adiam greve para fim de setembro
observador.description: Greve de pilotos marcada para domingo e segunda-feira foi suspensa. Sindicato diz que surgiu oportunidade para retomar negociações, mas mantém-se "vigilante".

observador.title: Reform recebe 84 milhões de dois milionários das 'cripto'
observador.description: Farage diz-se "honrado e humilde". Trabalhistas querem limitar donativos a 100 mil libras com efeitos retroativos. Ben Delo foi condenado por branqueamento de capitais e perdoado por Trump.

observador.title: Sociais-Democratas vencem eleições na Suécia
observador.description: Primeiras projeções dão vitória aos Sociais-Democratas com 28% dos votos. Extrema-direita tem resultado aquém das sondagens. Coligação de esquerda para governar é cenário mais provável.

spiegel.title: US Open im Liveticker: Alexander Zverev eröffnet vierten Satz gegen Ben Shelton mit einem Break
spiegel.description: Die direkte Antwort nach dem Satzverlust: Dank eines Breaks zu Beginn des vierten Satzes rückt der Titelgewinn für Alexander Zverev näher. Verfolgen Sie hier das Duell mit Ben Shelton im Live-Kommentar.

spiegel.title: Schweden-Wahl: Sozialdemokraten stärkste Kraft – Ausgang offen
spiegel.description: Schwedens Sozialdemokraten holen laut einer Hochrechnung 27,6 Prozent der Stimmen. Entgegen einer früheren Prognose unterliegt das linke Lager aber offenbar dem Mitte-rechts-Bündnis des amtierenden Regierungschefs.

spiegel.title: Basketball-WM: USA holen Titel trotz 14-Punkte-Rückstand gegen Frankreich
spiegel.description: USA, USA, USA, USA, USA. Zum fünften Mal in Folge haben sich die US-Basketballerinnen den Weltmeistertitel gesichert. Gegen Frankreich lag eine Sensation in der Luft.

spiegel.title: CDU laut Hochrechnung vor SPD – AfD und Linke legen zu
spiegel.description: Die CDU bleibt in Niedersachsen die stärkste Kraft, dazugewinnen konnten aber nur AfD und Linke. Nach dem Wahl-Debakel in Sachsen-Anhalt gelten die Kommunalwahlen als wichtiger Stimmungstest in Westdeutschland.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz: »Mit diesem Bundeskanzler sind keine Wahlen mehr zu gewinnen«
spiegel.description: Clara von Nathusius, Schatzmeisterin der Jungen Union, rät Friedrich Merz, er solle »nicht noch mal antreten«. Für Sondierungsgespräche mit der AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt zeigt sie sich offen.

spiegel.title: Ultimate Championship: Emil Agyekum pulverisiert deutschen Rekord über 400 Meter Hürden
spiegel.description: Mehr als 40 Jahre hatte der deutsche Rekord von Harald Schmid über 400 Meter Hürden Bestand, bevor ihn Emil Agyekum unterbot. Zum Saisonabschluss hat der 27-Jährige die Bestmarke nun noch mal gewaltig gesteigert.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump und Großbritannien: Was planen Wales, Schottland und Nordirland?
spiegel.description: Am Montag wollen die Regierungschefs der drei Landesteile über ihr Recht auf Unabhängigkeit beraten. Der Druck auf den britischen Premier Burnham steigt – auch weil sich US-Präsident Trump einmischt.

spiegel.title: Bier aus Deutschland: Schwester Doris, die letzte Klosterbraumeisterin in Mallersdorf
spiegel.description: Im niederbayerischen Mallersdorf führt Schwester Doris die letzte Brauerei, die noch zu einem Nonnenkloster gehört. Was ein gutes Bier ausmacht – und warum sie Nullpromille-Propheten wie Eckart von Hirschhausen verachtet.

spiegel.title: FC Bayern München siegt bei der SV Elversberg
spiegel.description: Zwei Siege legte Bundesliganeuling SV Elversberg zum Saisonstart hin. Auch gegen Rekordmeister FC Bayern spielte der Aufsteiger gut mit, musste sich aber der Klasse von Harry Kane geschlagen geben.

spiegel.title: Niedersachsen-Kommunalwahl: Grüner OB Belit Onay in Hannover liegt vorn
spiegel.description: Der amtierende Oberbürgermeister von Hannover, Belit Onay von den Grünen, kommt laut Zwischenergebnis auf rund 45 Prozent der Stimmen. Damit setzt er sich klar gegen seinen SPD-Stellvertreter Axel von der Ohe durch.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump gibt Ukraine die Schuld an steigenden Spritpreisen - trotz Lage in Nahost
spiegel.description: Die Angriffe der Huthi-Milizen auf Ölanlagen in Saudi-Arabien belasten den Benzin- und Dieselmarkt. Doch der US-Präsident sieht die Verantwortung woanders.

spiegel.title: Signal-Chefin Meredith Whittaker: »KI ist nicht menschlich«
spiegel.description: Die KI-Expertin Meredith Whittaker erklärt den DEIN-SPIEGEL-Kinderreportern, welche Aufgaben wir der KI nicht überlassen sollten – und wie eine Sicherheitslücke bei Google sie zur Datenschützerin machte.

spiegel.title: OpenAI: KI-Agenten griffen offenbar Plattform RubyGems an
spiegel.description: Monate vor dem Angriff auf Hugging Face stürmten KI-Agenten von OpenAI offenbar eine andere Internetplattform. Ein junger Forscher aus Bielefeld entdeckte die Spur – und sieht den Vorfall als Vorboten eines größeren Problems.

spiegel.title: Wie groß ist die Summe der Winkel? – Rätsel der Woche

phys-org.title: Astronomers unmask a supernova impostor
phys-org.description: A distant star has captured astronomers' attention over the past decade, teasing them with indications that it will soon explode as a supernova. But new research shows that something else entirely is behind the star's outbursts. Rather than an impending catastrophic explosion, a previously unseen companion may be responsible for the star's behavior.

phys-org.title: AI helps microscopes find the most informative nanoscale features in a sample
phys-org.description: Researchers at the Department of Energy's Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) have developed an artificial intelligence framework that helps researchers use atomic force microscopes to identify important nanoscale features while autonomously targeting the most informative areas of a sample for closer study.

phys-org.title: Masked tectonic structures suggest Mercury contracted 40% more than its visible scars alone indicate
phys-org.description: The surface of Mercury is filled with craters, ridges and steep cliffs. Over billions of years, as the planet's interior cooled, the planet also shrank. Just as the skin of a drying fruit wrinkles when what is inside it shrinks, Mercury's rocky surface crumpled into ridges and cliffs as its interior cooled and the planet contracted. Mercury has quite literally grown smaller with age.

phys-org.title: AI automates 3D membrane mapping, matching manual results in a fraction of time
phys-org.description: Cell membranes and the proteins within them control many vital processes and play a key role in health and disease. But studying them in 3D images of cells has so far meant slow, manual work. A team from Helmholtz Munich, the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and the Biozentrum of the University of Basel has developed MemBrain v2, an AI tool that automates this task—cutting work that once took weeks down to a few hours. The study is published in Nature Methods.

phys-org.title: Saltwater flooding could radically change which crops are worth growing
phys-org.description: Saltwater isn't something most people associate with English farmland. But in parts of eastern England, it's becoming a growing problem, not just for crops but for farm incomes too.

phys-org.title: Luminescence dating pushes age of South Dakota's Mammoth Site back by more than 100,000 years
phys-org.description: Deep within an ancient sinkhole lie the remains of dozens of mammoths, prehistoric wanderers who waded into the warm springs to their deaths. These deaths had long been accepted as having occurred roughly 26,000 years ago, but new dates published in the journal Quaternary Research suggest these ice-age giants were more than 160,000 years old.

phys-org.title: The tourism industry is slowly waking up to solo travelers' needs
phys-org.description: Solo travel is surging—and an industry still largely built for two is taking note. Google reported in April 2026 that online searches involving "solo travel" hit an all-time high this year, with queries for "women solo travel" reaching a 15-year peak. Hilton's 2026 trends report found that 26% of travelers planned to take a trip alone this year and that nearly half said they planned to add solo days to the front or back of a family trip.

phys-org.title: Gravitational-wave analysis narrows the search for black hole impostors
phys-org.description: Black holes are regions of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape. When two black holes orbit each other and merge, they produce gravitational waves (i.e., ripples in spacetime) that can resemble those emitted by mergers involving other exotic compact objects.

phys-org.title: Fish may be highly sensitive to antidepressants found in water
phys-org.description: Many of the drugs that target human brain chemistry, such as antidepressants, are still biologically active when they leave the body. These substances and their metabolites can persist in wastewater and eventually end up in the sea, rivers or other aquatic environments.

phys-org.title: Cataract surgery will be needed in space, surgeon predicts
phys-org.description: An eye surgeon with a passion for space since childhood predicts that as astronauts start to make journeys to the moon and Mars in the near future, eye surgery in space will eventually become a necessity.

phys-org.title: A 1,000-fold longer charge lifetime helps organic catalyst produce solar hydrogen faster
phys-org.description: Researchers from the Ningbo Institute of Materials Technology and Engineering (NIMTE) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), in collaboration with researchers from the Technical Institute of Physics and Chemistry of CAS, have developed a coumarin-linked covalent organic framework (COF) that enables high-efficiency photocatalytic water splitting for hydrogen production.

phys-org.title: NASA's next great observatory could spot oceans on distant worlds
phys-org.description: We've found more than 5,500 exoplanets so far. Dozens of them are in the habitable zones of their parent stars, where, at least in theory, they could host an ocean. But we've never definitively found a liquid ocean on another planet.

phys-org.title: Researchers pinpoint key early-universe measurement with record precision
phys-org.description: An international team, including researchers from the University of Minnesota Twin Cities, has reached a major milestone in "precision cosmology" by measuring the amount of helium created in the universe's first five minutes with unprecedented accuracy.

phys-org.title: Ancient armored fish evolved two distinct ways to crush prey 385 million years ago
phys-org.description: Long before dinosaurs appeared on Earth, fierce predatory fish developed crushing jaws and sharp teeth to survive and diversify in ancient oceans.

phys-org.title: AI could make holiday planning easier for overwhelmed travelers
phys-org.description: Generative AI could help overwhelmed travelers organize their thoughts, compare options and complete vacation plans they might otherwise abandon, according to new research from the University of Surrey.

phys-org.title: Magnetic nanoparticles detect amoxicillin allergy with 98% sensitivity in early tests
phys-org.description: A multidisciplinary scientific team at the University of Malaga has developed a new technology based on magnetic nanoparticles that enables precise, rapid and reliable diagnosis of allergy to beta-lactam antibiotics, including amoxicillin and other penicillins.

phys-org.title: Six ways people have used magic to protect their homes throughout history—from witch bottles to 'hag stones'
phys-org.description: Virtually all cultures and eras fizz with magic. You might call it a secret ingredient of human life because magic takes so many forms and serves so many functions.

phys-org.title: Japan's Hayabusa2 achieves first-ever laser ranging experiment with an asteroid
phys-org.description: The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's (JAXA) Hayabusa2 spacecraft reached another milestone this summer, a first for space agencies. On Sunday, July 5, the probe conducted the first successful laser-ranging experiment during a flyby of asteroid Torifune, the first exploration target of Hayabusa2's Extended Mission. This latest milestone will advance the capabilities of JAXA and other space agencies as they pursue future missions involving near-Earth asteroids (NEAs) and other deep-s

undark.title: Review: A Vision of a Future Where Machines Fight Wars
undark.description: In “Lethal Autonomy,” Frank Kendall, a former top defense department official, envisions a military future where vehicles and weapons operate largely on their own — including making some decisions to strike people or infrastructure. And in his view, conflict is coming to space, making it all more urgent.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

proj-syn.title: The Program Redesign the IMF Needs
proj-syn.description: The International Monetary Fund’s guidelines for program design are more salient than ever, given widespread debt distress in developing countries. As the Fund undertakes its first major evaluation since 2019, it should focus on three features of its lending, all of which need to be reformed.

proj-syn.title: AI Could Make Governments Slower
proj-syn.description: Governments are increasingly turning to AI tools to process vast amounts of information and make public services more efficient. But because human attention is finite, making machines more capable could simply create new bottlenecks wherever oversight is necessary.

proj-syn.title: Why Do So Few Women Work in India?
proj-syn.description: India’s female labor force participation rate has long lagged behind that of peer economies like Bangladesh, not because of social norms, but because of weak demand for labor. That is ultimately good news, because it is a problem that can be solved with common-sense regulatory reforms and public investment.

proj-syn.title: Global Development’s Missing Ingredient
proj-syn.description: Facing a democracy deficit worldwide, millions of vulnerable people lack avenues through which they can collectively negotiate their interests. Faith-based institutions committed to human dignity and pluralism can play an instrumental role in building the infrastructure required for grassroots organizing at scale.

proj-syn.title: China’s External Surplus Makes a “Mandarin Accord” Inevitable
proj-syn.description: As with the Plaza Accord in 1985, when the United States and its major trading partners agreed to coordinate policies to weaken the US dollar, an agreement to address global imbalances emanating from China has become increasingly necessary. Given China’s undervalued currency, the situation simply cannot be sustained indefinitely.

proj-syn.title: War and Climate
proj-syn.description: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz showed how quickly a regional conflict can throw global energy markets into chaos. By pushing governments toward coal and biofuels, the war could accelerate deforestation and undermine climate negotiations, with environmental consequences that will linger long after the fighting ends.

proj-syn.title: 9/11’s Long Shadow
proj-syn.description: As tragic as the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, were, it was America’s response that truly changed the world. While it is difficult to pinpoint precisely which developments over the last 25 years were caused or compounded by 9/11, it seems clear that the event led the United States to abandon the principles that, with the Cold War over, were supposed to shape a better future.

proj-syn.title: The False Politics of Western Declinism
proj-syn.description: Political leaders on both sides of the Atlantic increasingly portray the West as being in decline, even as their societies grow richer. By conflating a loss of relative economic power with falling living standards, they give populists an opening to turn domestic grievances into nationalist resentment.

proj-syn.title: What 9/11 Did to Us
proj-syn.description: For Americans who are old enough to remember them, the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks raised fundamental questions: Who could have done this, and above all, why? We now know that the answers would reshape the country and its place in the world—and not for the better.

proj-syn.title: After the AI Bubble Bursts
proj-syn.description: Just as debt markets fueled the global financial near-meltdown that followed the 2007–08 subprime-mortgage crisis, their exposure to AI will drive developments now. The problem is that we possess only very limited public information about those markets, and regulators are not making that information any easier to obtain.

proj-syn.title: Trump Is Stoking Territorial Revisionism
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump’s refusal to respect international borders has already led Argentina and Morocco to revive territorial disputes and has effectively given Israel carte blanche to operate where it sees fit. But this might be just the beginning: if the US can claim land and resources on the basis of vague national-security claims, anyone can.

proj-syn.title: Have the Terrorists Won?
proj-syn.description: The point of terrorism is not to cause suffering, but to provoke the target into doing something that hurts it even more. In the quarter-century since the 9/11 attacks, the US has done just that, leaving the world and itself worse off.

proj-syn.title: How 9/11 Fractured the Global Order
proj-syn.description: The terrorist attack on the United States 25 years ago remains among the most consequential events of this century. By fundamentally altering the trajectories of the United States and Russia, as well as that of a rising China, al-Qaeda’s attack set in motion developments that would produce the geopolitical tumult we live in today.

proj-syn.title: China’s Permanent Manufacturing Revolution
proj-syn.description: In developed economies, manufacturing employment will decline, regardless of industrial strategies pursued. China's competitiveness means that any expectation that manufacturing will absorb more than a trivial fraction of the large increases in the working-age population still occurring in India or Africa is a delusion.

proj-syn.title: Europe Needs Dual-Use Defense Spending
proj-syn.description: Some EU countries, such as Poland, are using their expanded defense budgets to buy more foreign hardware. A better approach would be to foster a thriving innovation ecosystem which ensures that the technologies, institutions, and people that underpin a strong military benefit the civilian economy as well.

proj-syn.title: The World 9/11 Didn’t Make
proj-syn.description: Looking back at the past quarter-century, it becomes apparent that the 9/11 terrorist attack against the United States was not a transformative event. Far more important developments have intervened, not least America’s rejection of the postwar order that it had a large hand in building.

proj-syn.title: The BRICS at 20
proj-syn.description: If the promise of the BRICS was to establish a monetary union, a single market, or a tightly integrated political alliance, it has not been fulfilled. But if it was to build a platform for emerging economies to cooperate while advancing their own strategic autonomy, the BRICS has exceeded expectations.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: The Boring Co., Cognition And Motive Lead A Massive Week
crunchbase.description: It was a monster week for U.S. startup funding, with four companies each raising $1 billion or more. The Boring Co. led with a $3 billion Series D, followed by AI coding startup Cognition at $2 billion. Joining them near the top was fleet management software provider Motive, which landed $1.3 billion, while reusable rocket developer Stoke Space raised another $1 billion.

crunchbase.title: The Only 2 Moats That Actually Work In The AI Era
crunchbase.description: AI itself is no longer a durable differentiator, argues guest author SC Moatti of Mighty Capital, who says he strongest startup moats are counter-positioning and network economies.

crunchbase.title: How This Doctor-Turned-Startup-Founder Decided To Fix The Healthcare Staffing Crunch: Make Employers Apply
crunchbase.description: Iman Abuzeid left clinical medicine to tackle healthcare problems at scale, co-founding Incredible Health, a hiring platform that reverses traditional recruiting by having employers apply to healthcare professionals by combining her expertise with co-founder Rome Portlock’s technical skills the company uses AI agents to cut hiring time by 30%.

crunchbase.title: How To Measure An Innovation Economy: South Korea
crunchbase.description: Guest author Alberto Onetti, chairman of Mind the Bridge, shares how South Korea’s rise to the world’s eighth-largest national innovation ecosystem shows how sustained government investment, startup programs, regulatory reforms and deep-tech policies can transform an economy over time.

crunchbase.title: 29 Companies Joined The Unicorn Board In August, Led By AI Software And Semiconductors
crunchbase.description: A total of 29 companies joined The Crunchbase Unicorn Board in August, adding around $63 billion in value to the board. More than a third of the companies to join last month were under 3 years old, underscoring how quickly some of today's best-funded startups are reaching multibillion-dollar valuations.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker
crunchbase.description: Over 127,000 workers at U.S.-based tech companies were laid off in mass job cuts in 2025, per a Crunchbase News tally, and the layoffs have continued into 2026. See the latest companies to cut roles.

crunchbase.title: The Sales Test This Norwest Partner Gives Founders Before He’ll Invest
crunchbase.description: In an interview with Crunchbase News, Sean Jacobsohn, a partner at venture firm Norwest, discusses where he still sees openings in the crowded market for finance software, how far companies should trust AI with accounting work, why HR startups may be better off attacking the secondary products of large platforms, and why he tests a CEO's sales ability before investing.

crunchbase.title: Mistral AI Raises $3.5B At $24B Valuation In Another Record European AI Round
crunchbase.description: Paris-based generative AI startup Mistral AI said Tuesday that it has nearly doubled its valuation to more than $24 billion with a Samsung Electronics-led $3.5 billion Series D fundraise.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Crusoe And Fluidstack Lead Multibillion-Dollar AI Infrastructure Haul
crunchbase.description: AI infrastructure dominated the largest venture rounds this week, with two multibillion-dollar deals in the sector taking the top spots. Data center and cloud provider Crusoe led with a massive $3 billion financing, followed by Fluidstack’s $1.5 billion raise.

crunchbase.title: A Startup General Counsel Knew What Corporate Lawyers Needed From AI. So She Built It.
crunchbase.description: After nearly two decades working as a lawyer at companies such as Amazon, Cruise, Replit and Anki, Cecilia Ziniti teamed up with engineer Bardia Pourvakil to combine their knowledge of law and coding to co-found GC AI.
